title: Yonsei University Brings IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 Online in First International On-Premises Deployment - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM's Nighthawk r2 processor (120 programmable qubits on a square lattice, >100,000 circuits/s) went live at Yonsei University's Songdo campus, replacing a 127-qubit Eagle and marking the first on-premises Nighthawk deployment outside the US. The ~25x throughput gain is aimed at high-depth error-mitigated workloads for Yonsei's Bio-Quantum Initiative.

insights.claim: Yonsei University and IBM activated an IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor inside the IBM Quantum System One at the Songdo International Campus, the first deployment of the Nighthawk architecture at an on-premises client facility outside the United States.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows IBM's newest QPU is moving into international on-prem installs, extending its hardware-sales footprint beyond cloud access.
insights.quote: the world’s first deployment of IBM’s Nighthawk architecture at an on-premises client facility outside the United States
insights.locator: South Korea’s Yonsei University and IBM

insights.claim: IBM Nighthawk r2 provides 120 programmable qubits within a 458-physical-qubit square lattice that includes 218 tunable couplers and reset elements, replacing the 127-qubit heavy-hexagonal IBM Eagle installed at Yonsei in 2024.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM is trading raw qubit count for connectivity and quality, signaling the metric that matters is shifting from qubit numbers to usable circuit depth.
insights.locator: Yonsei IBM Quantum System One: Hardware Architecture

insights.claim: Fast active qubit reset lifts circuit execution throughput on the Yonsei system from about 4,000 to more than 100,000 circuits per second, roughly a 25x acceleration.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Throughput gains directly cut the cost per useful sample, which is the binding constraint for error-mitigated workloads.
insights.quote: ~25× throughput acceleration enabled by fast active qubit reset
insights.locator: Yonsei IBM Quantum System One: Hardware Architecture

insights.claim: Nighthawk r2 has demonstrated accurate observable estimation beyond 7,500 gates, satisfying IBM's 2026 technical roadmap target.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: IBM hitting its own roadmap milestone on schedule supports credibility of its later fault-tolerance timeline.
insights.quote: Accurate observable estimation demonstrated beyond 7,500 gates (satisfying IBM’s 2026 technical roadmap target)
insights.locator: Yonsei IBM Quantum System One: Hardware Architecture

insights.claim: By adding tunable couplers and fast-reset auxiliary circuits, the square-lattice Nighthawk r2 design suppresses idle crosstalk and shortens the shot-repetition cycle time compared with the heavy-hexagonal Eagle layout.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Explains the mechanism behind IBM's performance jump, useful for comparing superconducting vendors' architectural choices.
insights.quote: Nighthawk r2 suppresses idle crosstalk and dramatically curtails the shot-repetition cycle time
insights.locator: The upgrade transitions the Songdo facility

insights.claim: A local execution rate of 100,000 circuits per second gives on-premises researchers the sample collection rates needed for high-depth variational algorithms and error-mitigated workflows without the queue overheads of cloud access.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Supports the case that research institutions will keep buying dedicated on-prem quantum systems rather than relying solely on cloud time.
insights.quote: without incurring prohibitive cloud queue overheads
insights.locator: The upgrade transitions the Songdo facility

insights.claim: Yonsei's on-prem system is an upgradable installation: the Eagle processor commissioned in 2024 was swapped for Nighthawk r2 within about two years, creating a recurring hardware-refresh relationship with IBM.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Processor swaps inside installed System One units suggest a recurring upgrade revenue model for IBM's on-prem business.
insights.locator: South Korea’s Yonsei University and IBM

insights.claim: Since commissioning its original System One, the Yonsei research community has produced over a dozen peer-reviewed studies on IBM hardware, including a 104-qubit study of error-mitigated quench dynamics in Heisenberg spin chains published in Physica Scripta.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Measurable research output is the justification for on-prem system purchases and for follow-on upgrades.
insights.quote: the Yonsei research community has generated over a dozen peer-reviewed studies on IBM hardware
insights.locator: Since commissioning the original System One

insights.claim: Yonsei researchers ran a 44-qubit hybrid quantum-classical simulation of the pyridine–Li+ complex using Qunova's Hi-VQE Qiskit Function on IBM hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Third-party software such as Qunova's is being distributed through IBM's Qiskit Functions channel, a sign of an emerging app-layer ecosystem.
insights.locator: Since commissioning the original System One

insights.claim: The Nighthawk r2 at Yonsei will primarily support the Yonsei Bio-Quantum Initiative, applying hybrid quantum-classical workflows to mitochondrial electron transport chain mutations, Leigh Syndrome modeling, neurodegenerative disorders and industrial materials discovery.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Life-sciences use cases are being positioned as the anchor workload for national on-prem quantum installs.
insights.locator: Since commissioning the original System One
